predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Duklja as a Byzantine province: toparchy 'of the Dalmatian kastra of Zeta and Ston' held by Vojislav, who revolted c.

successors.name: Kingdom of Serbia (Nemanjić state)
successors.text: Duklja's territory annexed by Stefan Nemanja in 1186

ledger.x: c. 1034: Stefan Vojislav revolts and Duklja breaks from Byzantium. 'Following John Skylitzes, Duklja's break from Byzantine rule is dated to about this time'; the Duklja page has him seize Duklja in 1034; he had been Byzantine 'toparch of Zeta and Ston' since 1018.
c. 1034: the Byzantine war for Duklja begins. Vojislav is 'defeated and imprisoned in Constantinople in 1035/1036', escapes 'in late 1037 or early 1038' and 'liberated most of Duklja' (Duklja page).
By 1040: Vojislav holds the coast from Ston to Skadar.
1060s: Mihailo conquers Raska from the Byzantines.
1077: Mihailo receives a crown from Pope Gregory VII and Duklja becomes a kingdom.
After 1090: Zahumlje and Bosnia break away.
1150: Raska's Desa appears as ruler of Duklja.
1186: the last Doclean land passes to Nemanja's Serbia.

wars.name: Revolt of Stefan Vojislav against Byzantium
wars.outcome: Vojislav is defeated and imprisoned in 1035/1036, escapes in 1037/1038, liberates most of Duklja and defeats the Byzantine coalition between Bar and Crmnica in 1042.

wars.name: Uprising of Georgi Voiteh (Bodin's expedition)
wars.outcome: Mihailo sends Bodin with 300 troops; Bodin is crowned emperor of the Bulgarians as Petar, takes part in the revolt in Pomoravlje and Povardarje, is captured and freed in 1078; no border change.

wars.name: Byzantine punishment of Bodin
wars.outcome: The Byzantines, after dealing with the Normans, defeat Bodin and imprison him again; Raska, Zahumlje and Bosnia probably break away after 1090.

wars.name: Succession wars after Bodin and Raska's intervention
wars.outcome: Dobroslav II, Kocopar, Vladimir and Djuradj contend; Vukan of Raska helps Kocopar defeat Dobroslav then drives Kocopar out; the Byzantines install Grubesa in 1118 (to 1125); Uros of Raska restores Djuradj.

certainty.note: The Chronicle of the Priest of Duklja is a disputed source for the extent under Mihailo and Bodin; no treaty lines are on the pages opened, so the Bosnian and Rascian marches are approximate throughout.
